# Lockflight gates for Azure Pipelines — generated by `lockflight init --ci-platform azure`. The policy and the engine pin
# (.lockflight/engine.lock) are read from the target branch's tip on pull requests, not the pull request. The verdict is a
# strong guardrail, not a boundary: it blocks a merge only where a build validation policy requires it. Create a pipeline from this
# file and make it a build validation policy on main; route this file to a required reviewer. Not yet verified on a live
# Azure DevOps organisation: check the first run. See docs/guides/ci-other-platforms.md in the Lockflight repository.
# On Azure Repos the pr block is ignored: a build validation policy on main runs this pipeline for every pull request.
trigger:
  branches:
    include: [main]
pr:
  branches:
    include: ['*']

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

variables:
  GITLEAKS_VERSION: 8.30.1
  GITLEAKS_SHA256: 551f6fc83ea457d62a0d98237cbad105af8d557003051f41f3e7ca7b3f2470eb

steps:
  - checkout: self
    fetchDepth: 0
  - bash: |
      set -e
      if [ "$BUILD_REASON" = "PullRequest" ]; then
        # Policy comes from the target branch's tip, not the merge base: a branch cut from an old commit must not bring
        # an older engine pin, baselines or analyzer config. The gates work out the merge base themselves.
        target="${SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_TARGETBRANCH#refs/heads/}"
        git fetch --quiet origin "+refs/heads/$target:refs/remotes/origin/$target"
        BASE=$(git rev-parse "origin/$target")
      else
        BASE=$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet 'HEAD^' || true)
      fi
      echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=LOCKFLIGHT_BASE]$BASE"
    displayName: Find the base commit
  - bash: |
      set -e
      BASE="$LOCKFLIGHT_BASE"
      for file in dotnet-tools.json .config/dotnet-tools.json lockflight.yaml .lockflight/engine.lock .gitleaks.toml .gitleaksignore nuget.config NuGet.config NuGet.Config; do
        if git cat-file -e "$BASE:$file" 2>/dev/null; then mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")"; rm -f "$file"; git show "$BASE:$file" > "$file"; else rm -f "$file"; fi
      done
      # Accepted baselines (known-failing tests, warnings, advisories) are policy too: a PR cannot accept its own failures. So is
      # the vendored engine install script: CI runs the base commit's copy, checked against the base commit's lock.
      for directory in .lockflight/baselines .lockflight/ci; do
        rm -rf "$directory"
        if git cat-file -e "$BASE:$directory" 2>/dev/null; then
          git -c core.quotePath=false ls-tree -r --name-only "$BASE" -- "$directory" | while IFS= read -r file; do mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")"; rm -f "$file"; git show "$BASE:$file" > "$file"; done
        fi
      done
      # Code-style and analyzer config (nested files too) decides what the build and format gates enforce: a PR is
      # judged by the base's rules, and its own rule changes apply after the merge.
      style='(^|/)(\.editorconfig|\.globalconfig|[^/]*\.globalconfig|[^/]*\.ruleset|stylecop\.json|BannedSymbols\.txt|CodeMetricsConfig\.txt)$'
      { git ls-tree -r --name-only "$BASE"; git ls-files; } | { grep -E "$style" || true; } | sort -u | while IFS= read -r file; do
        if git cat-file -e "$BASE:$file" 2>/dev/null; then git checkout "$BASE" -- "$file"; else rm -f "$file"; fi
      done
    displayName: Use the base branch's engine pin and policy
    condition: and(succeeded(), eq(variables['Build.Reason'], 'PullRequest'))
  - bash: |
      set -e
      LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP="$AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY"
      archive="gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_linux_x64.tar.gz"
      curl -fsSLo "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/$archive" "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}/$archive"
      echo "$GITLEAKS_SHA256  $LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/$archive" | sha256sum -c -
      tar -xzf "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/$archive" -C "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP" gitleaks
      echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=LOCKFLIGHT_GITLEAKS]$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/gitleaks"
      gitleaks_sum=$(sha256sum < "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/gitleaks")
      echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=LOCKFLIGHT_GITLEAKS_SHA256;isreadonly=true]${gitleaks_sum%% *}"
    displayName: Install gitleaks (pinned, checksum-verified)
  - task: UseDotNet@2
    displayName: Install .NET 8.0.x
    inputs:
      packageType: sdk
      version: 8.0.x
  - task: UseDotNet@2
    displayName: Install .NET 10.0.x
    inputs:
      packageType: sdk
      version: 10.0.x
  - bash: |
      set -e
      LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP="$AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY"
      # lockflight:install-engine:begin
      if [ -f .config/dotnet-tools.json ]; then manifest=.config/dotnet-tools.json; else manifest=dotnet-tools.json; fi
      pinned=$( { tr -d '\r\n' < "$manifest" 2>/dev/null || true; } | grep -oiE '"lockflight\.cli"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\{[^}]*\}' | grep -oE '"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' | sed -E 's/.*"([^"]*)"$/\1/' || true)
      if [ -f .lockflight/engine.lock ]; then
        expected=$(sed -n 's/.*"installScript"[^}]*"sha256"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)".*/\1/p' .lockflight/engine.lock)
        if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then actual=$(sha256sum < .lockflight/ci/install.sh); else actual=$(shasum -a 256 < .lockflight/ci/install.sh); fi
        if [ -z "$expected" ] || [ "${actual%% *}" != "$expected" ]; then echo "lockflight: .lockflight/ci/install.sh is not the script .lockflight/engine.lock pins" >&2; exit 1; fi
        locked=$(sed -n 's/^  "version":[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' .lockflight/engine.lock)
        if [ -n "$pinned" ] && [ "$pinned" != "$locked" ]; then echo "lockflight: $manifest pins $pinned but .lockflight/engine.lock pins $locked; they must agree" >&2; exit 1; fi
        set --
        if [ -z "${LOCKFLIGHT_NUGET_FEED:-}" ]; then for file in nuget.config NuGet.config NuGet.Config; do if [ -f "$file" ]; then set -- --via-dotnet --nuget-config "$PWD/$file"; fi; done; fi
        sh .lockflight/ci/install.sh --lock .lockflight/engine.lock --dir "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/lockflight" "$@"
        # A pull request that changes the lock: the proposed lock must match the hashes its release published, and where the
        # gh CLI has a token (GitHub) the release's attestation must verify. The reviewer reads "matches release vX".
        base="${BASE:-${LOCKFLIGHT_BASE:-}}"
        if [ -z "$base" ] && [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME:-}" = pull_request ]; then base=$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet 'HEAD^1' || true); fi
        if [ -n "$base" ] && git cat-file -e "$base:.lockflight/engine.lock" 2>/dev/null && git cat-file -e "HEAD:.lockflight/engine.lock" 2>/dev/null \
          && ! git diff --quiet "$base"...HEAD -- .lockflight/engine.lock; then
          git show HEAD:.lockflight/engine.lock > "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/proposed-engine.lock"
          git show "$base:.lockflight/engine.lock" > "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/base-engine.lock"
          # The pull request's own install script must be the one its lock pins: CI runs that script once it is merged.
          if ! git show HEAD:.lockflight/ci/install.sh > "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/proposed-install.sh" 2>/dev/null; then echo "lockflight: the changed .lockflight/engine.lock comes without .lockflight/ci/install.sh" >&2; exit 1; fi
          "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/lockflight/lockflight" engine verify-lock "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/proposed-engine.lock" --base "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/base-engine.lock" --script "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/proposed-install.sh" ${GH_TOKEN:+--attestation}
        fi
        # A pull request that removes the lock would have CI install the engine by version alone once it is merged.
        if [ -n "$base" ] && git cat-file -e "$base:.lockflight/engine.lock" 2>/dev/null && ! git cat-file -e "HEAD:.lockflight/engine.lock" 2>/dev/null; then echo "lockflight: this pull request removes .lockflight/engine.lock, which pins the engine by hash; without it CI would install the engine by version only" >&2; exit 1; fi
      else
        # The first lock (the move from a 0.2 tool pin) is judged by the base's 0.2 engine, which cannot check it against its release.
        if git cat-file -e "HEAD:.lockflight/engine.lock" 2>/dev/null; then echo "lockflight: WARNING: this pull request adds the first .lockflight/engine.lock, which CI on this platform does not check against its release; run 'lockflight engine verify-lock .lockflight/engine.lock' before you accept it" >&2; fi
        if [ -z "$pinned" ]; then echo "lockflight: neither .lockflight/engine.lock nor $manifest pins the engine; run lockflight init and commit the pin" >&2; exit 1; fi
        config=""
        for file in nuget.config NuGet.config NuGet.Config; do if [ -f "$file" ]; then config="$PWD/$file"; fi; done
        (cd "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP" && dotnet tool install Lockflight.Cli --tool-path "$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/lockflight" --version "$pinned" ${config:+--configfile "$config"})
      fi
      # lockflight:install-engine:end
      echo "##vso[task.prependpath]$LOCKFLIGHT_TEMP/lockflight"
    displayName: Install the pinned engine (outside the repository's global.json)
  - bash: |
      set -e
      BASE="$LOCKFLIGHT_BASE"
      if [ -z "$BASE" ] || ! git cat-file -e "$BASE^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then BASE=""; fi
      lockflight gate run --profile pr ${BASE:+--base "$BASE"} --result artifacts/lockflight/result.json
    displayName: Gates
  - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
    condition: always()
    continueOnError: true
    inputs:
      targetPath: artifacts/lockflight
      artifact: lockflight-result
